programme.desc: S6 E7 — VictorianIn a 'Bake Off' first, the entire episode is devoted to the period of history that gave birth to modern baking, the Victorians. The signature challenge is a stalwart of the Victorian dinner table, Game Pie.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S6 E8 — PatisserieThe bakers have to be tested on Pâtisserie and what better time to do it than the quarter-finals? The five remaining bakers must work their way through a wide range of childhood favourites, delicate French fancies and a mountainous choux pastry masterpiece.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E19 — CataloniaJames visits the Boqueria market in Catalonia, eats Catalan paella in Sitges, takes a tour of a cava vineyard, and sees how honey sweets are made. He cooks cod in a romesco sauce, spatchcock chicken, cannelloni, and fruit in cava crème anglaise.

programme.title: James Martin's Spanish Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E20 — GironaJames drops by an anchovy producer in Girona, sees how ratafia is made, meets an award-winning chocolatier, and visits the Celler de Can Roca. He cooks anchovy topped tortilla, walnut and orange cake, beef fillet and a final tribute to Spain, paella.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S40 E11 — Domestic & AbroadOn this trip, Guy Fieri's digging into all-American and foreign favourites. In Houston, TX, a funky spot is firing up Filipino flavour with a twist. Then, a real-deal Washington meat market is stacking up serious sandwiches.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S41 E1 — Regional FlavorsGuy Fieri digs into righteous regional flavours where you may not expect to find them, like Cajun jambalaya in Bend, Ore.; Pakistani oxtail in Chehalis, Wash.; a tiki joint in Houston serves elevated dumplings and honey butter chicken biscuits.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S41 E3 — Meat and HeatGuy Fieri rolls into a tucked-away panini paradise in Chehalis, Wash.; a Korean spot in Brentwood, Tenn., gets spicy with their chicken and bulgogi; in Houston, a barbecue joint throws Tex-Mex into the mix with brisket tacos and jalapeño sausage.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S41 E4 — Sandwiches and SpiceIn Bend, Ore., a bagel shop is loading up pastrami; a Venezuelan spot in Salt Lake City is making amazing arepas; a Nashville joint is putting their twist on Jamaican specialties.

programme.title: Mystery Diners
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Catering on the SideThe Groves Bar and Grill owner becomes concerned over a large loss in food and supplies, so the Mystery Diners go undercover with hidden cameras.

programme.title: Mystery Diners
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Bringing Down the HausThe owners of German restaurant Haus Murphy's in Arizona hire the mystery diners to go undercover to see how incompetent their nephew is as a manager.

programme.title: Cake Boss
programme.desc: S11 E3 — Naked FishingThings quickly get out-of-hand when Buddy fills an order for an ice-fishing cake. Meanwhile, an important client requests a naked cake and Buddy is not impressed.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers Go North
programme.desc: S1 E8 — Tyne and Wear/NewcastleThe Hairy Bikers explore a region close to Si's heart: Tyne and Wear and its great city of Newcastle, where he spent most of his life. After weeks travelling across the stunning northern countryside, the bikers are having an urban adventure.

programme.title: Delicious Miss Brown
programme.desc: S6 E8 — Pasta! Pasta!Kardea Brown makes an Italian meal for her pasta-loving friend. She starts with Homemade Pasta crafted by hand, whips up Carbonara sauce and Roasted Artichokes with Parmesan Breadcrumbs and serves creamy Panna Cotta topped with fresh berries.

programme.title: Delicious Miss Brown
programme.desc: S6 E11 — Dream RecipesKardea makes a few of her all-time favourite recipes that she would put in her own cookbook, including jerk chicken rasta pasta, country sloppy Joes with fried onions, frozen yogurt bark with strawberry-balsamic jam, and chocolate sandwich delights.

programme.title: Jamie's Money Saving Meals
programme.desc: S1 E5 — LambJamie cooks up a roast shoulder of lamb with all the trimmings and turns the leftovers into Moroccan-style crispy pastillas.

programme.title: Jamie's Money Saving Meals
programme.desc: S1 E6 — HamJamie cooks up pot roasted ham hocks with parsley sauce, and roasts a butternut squash which he turns into a squash and spinach rotolo.

programme.title: Barefoot Contessa: Back to Basics
programme.desc: S5 E6 — Beach Volleyball PicnicIna puts together a portable feast to eat at the beach while watching her friend's daughter play volleyball. She makes a high energy snack for the teams and lunch for the spectators. Recipes include curried chicken wraps, panzanella, and peanut butter and jelly bars.

programme.title: Barefoot Contessa: Back to Basics
programme.desc: S5 E7 — Barefoot ReunionIna marks the show's anniversary by rustling up some classic recipes for her original team, including barbecue ribs, potato salad, blue cheese coleslaw, and chocolate ganache cupcakes.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S6 E9 — ChocolateThe pressure is on as the remaining bakers must get to grips with the one of the most difficult ingredients, chocolate.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S6 E11 — The FinalOnly three of the original twelve bakers remain. They've made it to the final. Over 27 challenges, they've worked their way through every baking discipline Mary and Paul have thrown at them from cakes to bread, pastry to puddings, and biscuits to chocolate.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E15 — Laverstoke and GoodwoodJames is bringing his culinary tour of the UK to his neck of the woods as he spends precious time in his adopted home county of Hampshire. He's taking his gun dog Cooper to a training session at Laverstoke before cooking an amazing seasonal dish of partridge with vegetables and a sloe gin sauce. James hangs out with his best friend Jody Scheckter, an ex-Formula One racer with an epic car collection, and a surprising passion for buffalo mozzarella.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E16 — KentJames' culinary tour of Great Britain continues as he explores the South East and the county of Kent. Here he meets up with local chef and restaurateur Mark Sargeant. Mark grew up in Kent and now owns four restaurants across the county. James cooks on the regenerated Folkestone Harbour Arm, making his BBQ herring and salsa. Mark then visits Dockers Bakehouse and Brewery - his local sourdough and beer suppliers located in a shipping container.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: S22 E4 — Girls' Night InRee hosts a girls' night at the lodge, complete with a tasty spread of canapés and cocktails; her recipes include citrus shrimp nachos, courgette quinoa cakes with herbed yogurt, slow-cooker fondue, goat cheese truffles and butterfly martinis.

programme.title: Jamie Cooks Italy
programme.desc: S1 E1 — The Aeolian IslandsJamie Oliver kickstarts his new Italian cooking adventure on the Aeolian Islands, where he learns from locals how to cook stuffed squid, inspiring his grilled squid and zingy caper salsa. He also creates a Sunday lunch for all the family.

programme.title: Jamie Cooks Italy
programme.desc: S1 E2 — PugilaJamie Oliver heads to Puglia, one of the hottest food destinations in Italy, making hand-crafted pasta, a special seafood stew, and the region's answer to paella.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: S1 E7 — North East EnglandIn Wakefield, Rick meets Janet Oldroyd, whose family have been harvesting rhubarb for the past four generations, and they whip up a tasty rhubarb crumble. Then in Bradford, he discovers the perfect recipe for lamb karahi at a Karachi restaurant.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Food Heroes
programme.desc: S1 E8 — South East England & WalesRick and his little hairy friend, Chalky, pay a visit to Rick's favourite formal vegetable garden, at Chatsworth House. He crosses the River Severn to sample the delights of Wales, including cawl and Welsh Black cattle.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S32 E7 — Crazy Chicken and Twisted BurgersGuy Fieri's digging into crazy twists on chicken and burgers; in Wilmington, Del., there's a bourbon bar that's piling pork onto a patty and doctoring up chicken skins.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S41 E5 — Traditional TwistsBend, Ore., where a funky spot stuffs their buns with unexpected flavours; a Puerto Rican oasis in Utah cooks real deal mofongo, and a Nashville joint serves coal-fired pizza.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S41 E7 — Tacos, Tots and ChopsGuy Fieri enjoys a fun, filling fiesta, kicking off in Grand Junction, Colo., where a pub serves a real deal Reuben; a spot in Salt Lake City elevates tacos; an outrageous joint in Nashville, Tenn., cooks up Middle Eastern specialities.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S41 E8 — Classic and ComfortIn a classic, comfort-filled joyride, Guy Fieri finds mozzarella sticks and gravy fries at a retro diner in Leavenworth, Wash.; homestyle fried chicken and grits in Draper, Utah; and stellar meatless chorizo at a vegan spot in Nashville, Tenn.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Emily's David Bowie inspired dish celebrates Britain's food heroes and she's using Cornish duck meat from her local producer that she pairs with grilled radicchio and Malbec sauce. Joe has sourced his ingredients locally too, using hay from his family farm and Jersey beef.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs need to impress the esteemed judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver as well as a guest judge, one of the pop stars the banquet will celebrate. They are joined by one half of the synthpop duo The Communards, Reverend Richard Coles.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Tom `Westy' Westerland is a former National Chef of Wales and head chef of the Brasserie at Lucknam Park in Wiltshire. Cindy Challoner is the former head chef at prestigious teaching restaurant `The Classroom' in Cardiff. They face Andy Sheriden formerly of Sosban restaurant in Llanelli, returning to the competition for his second attempt at making it to the banquet.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Andy cooks venison in celebration of his favourite band, Oasis. He accompanies the loin with rhubarb and beetroot ketchup, black pudding purée, pickled beetroot and a pistachio crumb. Westy's beef dish `The Cow Shed' is named after a former stage at the Glastonbury festival.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from Wales must cook their four course menus again. They must take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their tributes to Britain's music success.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The three chefs begin by cooking their starters for a surprise veteran of the competition. Chris' dish `Brixton Academy Through the Years' is his refined take on the classic lamb, post gig junk food he ate after nights out at Brixton Academy.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Chris is cooking his interpretation of the classic beef dish Tournedos Rossini using guinea fowl. His inspiration is Proms in the Park and the British artists who mix classical and modern music styles. Alex's dish commemorates his late brother and the song by Northern Ireland artist DonnaTaggart that he associates with the difficult time of his death.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining chefs from Northern Ireland will recreate their four course menu for the esteemed judges: food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton and broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver. There's also a guest judge, one of the pop stars the banquet will celebrate.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs battle to get their starter course to the Abbey Road banquet and don't disappoint with stunning dishes dedicated to everything from Tom Jones to Grime. The rivals are cooking to impress food writer Matthew Fort, restaurateur Oliver Peyton, broadcaster and cook Andi Oliver, plus guest judge and British music legend Martin Kemp.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Some of the finest chefs in the UK compete to cook a fish course worthy of serving at a banquet celebrating the brilliance of British popular music, held at Abbey Road Studios. Along with the show's panel of expert judges, the rivals need to impress guest judge Kanya King.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The eight regional champions will compete to get their main courses onto the final menu of the banquet at Abbey Road Studios.They will be cooking for the judges food critic, Mathew Fort, cook and broadcaster Andi Oliver and restaurateur, Oliver Peyton plus guest judge, former Wham! star, Andrew Ridgeley. As ever, the judges will be looking for dishes laced with star quality and a good sprinkling of rock and roll wow factor worth of a banquet full of the music industry's finest.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Some of the country's finest chefs compete over the final place cooking at a banquet celebrating the brilliance of British popular music, held at Abbey Road studios. Each rival will need to cook a dessert to impress a panel of expert judges, along with guest judge Peter Hook, Joy Division and New Order bassist, and pioneer of Britain's Madchester scene.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs must cook in an unfamiliar kitchen and scale up their dishes to provide the highest calibre of dining for a full banquet room of diners. Their guests are celebrities and unsung heroes who have helped create British music's unparalleled global reputation.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The spotlight is on Scotland. Returning contenders Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway are all determined to get one of their dishes to the banquet. Will a witty take on spiced ham score highly, or will a warm chicken salad with a twist or a rabbit terrine come out on top? Veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE will be judging.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Returning contenders Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway cook their fish dishes. Will a traditional Scottish soup, a chowder or a risky no-cook mackerel dish impress veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The competition heats up as the three returning Scottish contenders, Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway, cook their main courses. An African inspired goat tagine, a beef dish inspired by a childhood cartoon and a duck dish with a comedy twist are dished up for veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Scottish returning contenders Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway have just one more chance to impress veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE and win their place in front of the judges. Will a comedy custard pie, a sophisticated chocolate dessert or doughnuts inspired by a Scottish tradition come out on top?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Only one chef can make it through to the national finals to represent Scotland and cook at a special banquet at the Royal Albert Hall.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The curtain raises on the competition in the North West. How will Aiden Byrne's dish entitled `Mad as a Box of Frogs' go down with veteran Phil Howard? Will he trounce Mary-Ellen McTague's crab starter or will Chris Holland's `Oriental style beef broth with a twis' score more highly with Phil?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The North West chefs cook their fish courses. Will Aiden Byrne's `The Culinary Joke' - a take on a classic prawn cocktail - raise a laugh, or will Mary-Ellen McTague's dish of dover sole or Chris Holland's `Gone Fishing' salmon dish prove winners?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs cook their main course. Will Aiden Byrne's witty beef dish entitled `Long Horn Beef with Noodle Pot' prove a winner, or will Mary-Ellen McTague's goat dish called `Our Kid' raise a smile? Perhaps Chris Holland will score highly with his dish called `A Tasting of Pork'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the chef's last chance to impress before the final two are chosen to face the `Great British Menu' judging panel. Which dessert will help get them through? Will it be Aiden Byrne's pineapple dish called `The Sweet Burger', Mary-Ellen McTague's take on a trifle called `Chamomile Lawn' or Chris Holland's dish called `Going Bananas'?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's decision time for the chefs from the North West. One chef has already left the competition and only two remain. The judges are joined by celebrity guest judge writer, presenter and performer Rowland Rivron.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: In central England, three culinary heavyweights return to the `Great British Menu' kitchen. Two Michelin star chef Daniel Clifford creates a dish called `A Trip to the Chippy', where nothing is as it first appears. That is also the theme for Michelin star chef Richard Bainbridge's starter, `banana split', while Will Holland offers up goats cheese mousse, balsamic jelly and gingerbread.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Here, the chefs try to impress with their fish courses. Daniel Clifford puts up a creative dish called `Catch of the Day'. Does Richard Bainbridge's dish titled `Tongue in Cheek' live up to its comedy name? Will judge Marcus Wareing find the comedy value in Will Holland's coconut poached brill, crab, celeriac and tomato essence?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs in central England cook their main courses. Daniel Clifford's main has the same title as Richard Bainbridge's fish course, `Tongue in Cheek', but it is a wildly different plate of food; Richard Bainbridge presents guinea fowl in a beef bladder and calls the dish `Which Came First: the Chicken or the Egg'; Will Holland offers roast longhorn beef rib eye, bread and bone marrow pudding and parsley paste.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs in central England have one last chance to impress Marcus Wareing before the final two are chosen to face the judging panel. Will Daniel Clifford's `Going Out with a Bang' be good enough? Has Richard Bainbridge dropped the comedy ball with his coffee and chocolate dessert called `Time to Reflect'? Or will an unusual dish of parsnip banoffee cake, chocolate tart and parsnip ice cream get Will Holland through?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's decision time for the chefs from the central England region. Only two chefs remain to cook their entire menus for judges Prue Leith, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. The panel is joined by guest judge, comedian and actor Jim Moir, known to millions as Vic Reeves.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs battle it out for a chance to cook at the special banquet. Will veteran judge Tom Kerridge like Chris Eden's modern twist on `Duck a l'Orange', or will he favour Peter Sanchez-Iglesias' dish called `Picnic'? Perhaps Emily Watkins's witty dish called `Eggs and Ham' will prove a winner.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs cook their fish courses here. Cornishman Chris Eden takes inspiration from home to create a lobster and oyster dish called `Gone Surfing', Peter Sanchez-Iglesias cooks up a dish inspired by childhood memories titled `Fish and Chips', while Emily Watkins serves up a dish with cured trout called `High Tea'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The South West chefs cook their main courses and veteran Tom Kerridge is looking for perfection. Will Chris Eden's spin on a fast food classic simply called `B.L.T' gain top points? Or will Peter Sanchez Iglesias' nostalgic dish `Roast Dinner' or Emily Watkins' venison dish `Shoot Lunch' prove a winner?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: For the South West chefs, which dessert will progress? Peach melba, apple pie and `Lolly and Sweets' fight it out.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's decision time for the chefs from the South West and only two remain. Who will cook their entire menus for the `Great British Menu' judges, Prue Leith, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton and their guest, writer and performer Simon Day? The judges aren't easily pleased and only world-class cooking will do.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Welsh chefs raise the curtain with their starters, but which one is going to produce a showstopper? All three contestants have created sophisticated plates of food with simple dish titles. Will veteran Jeremy Lee be impressed with Richard Davies's chicken salad or will Mary Ann Gilchrist's peas and ham or Luke Thomas's ham, egg and pineapple get them off to a flying start?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Welsh chefs cook their fish course. Richard Davies serves up grilled and tartare of mackerel, while Mary Ann Gilchrist serves a lobster dish and calls it `The Great Escape'. Luke Thomas is hoping that his quirky take on a classic fish finger will impress veteran Jeremy Lee too.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The Welsh chefs prepare their main courses, but will any of them impress veteran Jeremy Lee enough to give them a top score? Richard Davies's dish is simply called `A Tasting of Pork', Mary Ann Gilchrist's `Three's a Crowd' doesn't give much away, while Luke Thomas's dish is called `Beef, Bone Marrow and Watercress'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the final chance for the Welsh chefs to impress Jeremy Lee with their dessert dishes. Which creation will help get two chefs through to the judging show? Will it be Richard Davies's strawberries and cream with a Comic Relief twist, or will Mary Ann Gilchrist's `Some Like It Hot' or Luke Thomas's rhubarb and custard get them through?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Great British Menu continues as 24 of the nation's finest chefs battle it out to cook gastronomic masterpieces that are also witty and fun. Their dishes have to put a smile on faces as they compete for the prize of cooking a dish at a special banquet at the Royal Albert Hall celebrating 25 years of Comic Relief's Red Nose Day appeals. It is decision time for the chefs representing Wales.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Great British Menu continues as 24 of the nation's finest chefs battle it out to cook gastronomic masterpieces that are also witty and fun. programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three North East chefs all want to top the leader board on day one with their starter. How will Colin McGurran's tomato gazpacho and garden salad perform? Stephanie Moon thinks she also has a chance with a witty chicken dish called `Why Did the Chicken...', and Charlie Lakin offers a controversial duck dish called `Mind Your Step'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The North East chefs cook their fish courses. Will former champion Colin McGurran's dish of cockles and mussels with salmon, inspired by his childhood memories, also inspire veteran judge Jason Atherton? Or perhaps Stephanie Moon's fish dish with a nod to one of the most famous gags of all time, crab custard pie, will be the winner? Charlie Lakin is also confident with his creation called `Tongue in Cheek'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The North East chefs cook their main course and veteran Jason Atherton is looking for perfection. Will Colin McGurran's dish of duck and turnips be funnier than it sounds? Has Stephanie Moon dropped the comedy ball with her venison dish called `Behind the Fun is Some Serious Game'? Will Charlie Lakin's kebab inspired dish `A Night on the Tiles' raise a smile?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the North East chefs' last chance to impress before the final two are chosen to face the `Great British Menu' judging panel. Which desserts will help get two chefs through to the showdown? Will it be Colin McGurran's tiramisu, Stephanie Moon's tricky pulled sugar dome, or Charlie Larkin's custard pie?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's decision time for the chefs from the North East. One chef has already left the competition and only two remain. They must now cook their entire menus for the `Great British Menu' judges Prue Leith, Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and their guest, comedian Tim Brooke-Taylor. The judges aren't easily pleased and only world class cooking will do.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The curtain raises on the competition in Northern Ireland. How will Chris Fearon cope competing against his former head chef Raymond McArdle? Will rising star Ian Orr be caught up in the middle? Both Chris and Raymond create very different takes on soup while Ian comes up with a rabbit dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The three Northern Ireland chefs cook their fish courses. Chris Fearon serves up a creation called `Stitched up Like a Kipper', while Raymond McArdle draws inspiration from a view from home and serves turbot called `A Day at the Beach'. Ian Orr creates a dish with a play on an old joke called `Why Did the Scallop Cross the Roe'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's time for the main course. Chris Fearon's dish called `Cowboy Supper' is inspired by the Wild West. Raymond McArdle creates a dish called `Titanic Smoked Venison, Tongue and Cheek', and Ian Orr cooks lamb and baked hay.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the chefs' last chance to impress before the final two are chosen to face the `Great British Menu' judging panel. Which dessert will it be? Chris Fearon's dish inspired by comedy legend Tommy Cooper called `Just Like That?' competes against Raymond McArdle's `Chocolate Volcano Mountain' and Ian Orr's `Passion Egg'.

programme.title: Fred & Rose West: Love & Murder
programme.desc: Fred and Rose West raped, tortured and murdered at least a dozen young British girls between 1967 and 1987, including several of their own daughters. programme.title: Myra Hindley: The Untold Story

programme.title: Myra Hindley: The Untold Story

programme.title: Myra Hindley: The Untold Story
programme.desc: A look at the life and crimes of infamous killer Myra Hindley. This film explores the stories of Brady and Hindley's five known murder victims and the accounts of the children who got away, most notably David Smith.

programme.title: Infamous Crime Scenes: OJ
programme.desc: Turn back the clock and uncover the truth behind the OJ Simpson trial.

programme.title: Infamous Crimes: JFK
programme.desc: The story of JFK's assasination. He was an American politician who served as the 35th president of the United States from 1961 until his assassination near the end of his third year in office.

programme.title: Julian Assange: Free at Last
programme.desc: WikiLeaks, founded in 2006 by Julian Assange, became famous for exposing hidden secrets. Assange's 2019 arrest after years of asylum led to his imprisonment and espionage charges in the US, sparking global debates on press freedom, until his release in June 2024.

programme.title: The CEO Killer: Deny, Defend, Depose
programme.desc: Delving deep into the lives of Brian Thompson and Luigi Mangione, exploring their contrasting backgrounds, the events that drew them into each others orbit, and the shocking manifesto Mangione released that sent the internet into chaos.

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: A Miami river washes up a torso, leaving investigators baffled about where the remaining body parts are, or whether the person was male or female.

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: In New Mexico, police are called when 18-year-old Carly Martinez disappears from a local skating rink after a date with a friend.

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: When a car crashed down an embankment, rescue workers scrambled to save a couple trapped inside, but what followed was an unexpected twist.

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: A field becomes a graveyard in Ohio when a woman's body is discovered, but solving her murder means turning to a rare technique of fingerprinting..

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: When firefighters are called to a home in the middle of the night, they discover a fire raging out of control and a mystery woman's charred body.

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: When Hal cut off his wife's money to stop her partying, she left him. A look at whether there is enough evidence to convict the killer of a motel clerk.

programme.title: The New Detectives
programme.desc: Police search for a 22-year-old college student whose car was found abandoned outside Philadelphia. A 10-year-old boy is missing in Illinois.

programme.title: Holiday Love Rats Exposed
programme.desc: First of a three-part documentary series about people who have been conned out of money and left broken-hearted by someone they met on holiday.

programme.title: Holiday Love Rats Exposed
programme.desc: Three British women and an American describe how they met their husbands while they were abroad on holiday. One discovered that her husband was planning to leave her three years into their marriage after she had paid for his visa, while another reports that her ex-husband has asked her to look after his daughter from another marriage.

programme.title: Holiday Love Rats Exposed
programme.desc: Tracy, 54, travels to Turkey on a mission to get her money back from ex-lover Bulent, who has not paid back a business loan, and 51-year-old Anne Marie has over £14,000 of debt after being bamboozled by `Billy'.

programme.title: Fly Colt Fly: Legend of the Barefoot Bandit
programme.desc: Teenage fugitive Colton Harris-Moore becomes a modern folk hero after stealing a small plane and disappearing into the wilderness.

programme.title: Surviving Sinaga
programme.desc: Reynhard Sinaga is the UK's most prolific rapist. Meeting men outside Manchester nightclubs, he drugged, sexually assaulted and filmed his depraved acts with at least 200 young men for the past 12 years. Featuring interviews with those affected.

programme.title: Served: Harvey Weinstein
programme.desc: The rise and fall of one of Hollywood's most powerful men, Harvey Weinstein.

programme.title: Great Crimes and Trials

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E12The conflict in the Pacific provided history with some of the worst reminders of the true meaning of war. Even today the images captured on islands such as Iwo Jima and Okinawa have the power to shock a world by the horrors of more recent events.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E7Meanwhile in North Africa, the Italian dictator Mussolini had his own ideas about building a new Roman Empire in the region. And so he sent thousands of poorly-trained and ill-prepared Italian troops against the British garrison in Egypt.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E8This episode remembers some of the thunderous naval battles which took place during the Pacific war. They include the Battle of the Coral Sea, the battle of Midway and the biggest naval engagement of the war – the battle of Leyte Gulf.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E4The Russian soldier who led a desperate outbreak from a secret Nazi death camp, Operation Chicken - an audacious plan to flee an escape-proof Japanese prison camp, and the pilots whose bold bid for freedom won the admiration of their enemies.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II. Regarded as one of the most important aircraft of the Cold War. It was a major part of the United States Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and was also used by many other countries.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E1Examining moments of engineering ingenuity which made the difference between triumph and disaster on the battlefield - beginning with World War I.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E2Examining the machines used by iconic military unit 'The Desert Rats' in the North African desert campaign of World War II.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2The mighty Flying Fortress takes to the air as we examine the background and development of one of WWIIs most iconic bombers. Serving with both the USAAF and the RAF, we see it in action and fly a surfing example.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The F15 Eagle immediately turned the tide of the first Gulf War to prove its greatness. Our immaculately restored MiG Killer was involved in one of the most bizarre combat incidents during that conflict, and has survived to tell the tale.

programme.title: WWII Air Crash Detectives
programme.desc: E5A C-47 transport plane, with a crew of four, is ferrying 24 trainee P-47 fighter pilots from the Bruning Army Air Field in Nebraska to the South Dakotan Pierre Army Air Field for advanced training.

programme.title: WWII Air Crash Detectives
programme.desc: E6It is the 25th of August, 1942. A Short Sunderland Flying Boat slams into Eagle Rock, a remote hillside in the far north of Scotland, killing fourteen people on board. Miraculously, there is one survivor.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E1In the waters of Scapa Flow, discover sunken dreadnoughts that tell the story of how a U-Boat sank HMS Royal Oak. Later, on HMS Cavalier, we explore how a raid by commandos called Operation Chariot proved the vulnerability of the battleship.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E2The episode begins with the story of HMS Conqueror sinking the General Belgrano during the Falklands War. Later, a crew member from the USS Nautilus describes what it was like to serve on the world's first nuclear submarine.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II. Regarded as one of the most important aircraft of the Cold War. It was a major part of the United States Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and was also used by many other countries.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The Hawker Hurricane was the first RAF aircraft to fly over 300mph. Over half of every enemy aeroplane destroyed in the Battle of Britain was by a Hurricane, not a Spitfire.

programme.title: Iconic Combat Machines
programme.desc: E3Icons of the Royal Navy in different eras, the Belfast and the Harrier have earned their place in history for different reasons.

programme.title: Iconic Combat Machines
programme.desc: E4Two of the most produced combat machines in World War II managed to stay relevant until the end of the war through constant modernization and new variants.

programme.title: World War Weird
programme.desc: E1Near the Czech border, a secret German site, "The Giant," tests The Bell, powered by Serum 525, turning all who touch it into rotting living zombies.

programme.title: World War Weird
programme.desc: E21942 and Hitler has the totally barking idea of using educated dogs to do a soldier's job. The Nazi leader wants to create fearsome canines to help him win the Second World War.

programme.title: Hitler's Handmaidens
programme.desc: E1A look at the women surrounding Hitler once he came to power, and how they were held up as the Aryan Ideal to strive for once the Nazi dictator approved of their positions.

programme.title: Hitler's Handmaidens
programme.desc: E2How women were active - and often violent participants and perpetrators - in the conflict and its attendant atrocities - especially the Holocaust.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E3Weapons experts test the physical and psychological impact of close combat weapons - the Roman short sword, the medieval war hammer and the bayonet.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E4From the crossbow to the Kalashnikov to 3D-printed firearms, weaponry designed for everyone can offer a decisive advantage in warfare.

programme.desc: E1In the waters of Scapa Flow, discover sunken dreadnoughts that tell the story of how a U-Boat sank HMS Royal Oak. Later, on HMS Cavalier, we explore how a raid by commandos called Operation Chariot proved the vulnerability of the battleship.

programme.title: Commando Missions
programme.desc: E1In the north of Crete, six commandos land in a cove. On this island that has been occupied for two years, they have been given a high-risk mission—to infiltrate the Heraklion airfield to destroy the Luftwaffe bombers and fighter planes.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E3Examining the machines used by iconic military unit 'The Desert Rats' in the North African desert campaign of World War II.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E4We examine the robot that defused bombs both on foreign battlefields and British streets, and an astonishing Gulf War minelayer.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4Cruelly called 'the packing case the B17 came in,' the Liberator more than proved its worth over Europe and the Pacific, patterning the B17 to deliver a blow to the axis powers in WWII however it wasn't simply a bomb delivery system.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3Often called 'the forgotten bomber', the mighty North American twin delivered the first blow in the fight back against Japan, in one of the most daring and audacious raids of all time.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E3As the Third Reich rises to power, Himmler and the SS become fixated on the Holy Grail, interpreting much of the myth surrounding it as fact - and the quest for it as attainable.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E4A pseudoscientific theory embraced by the Nazis claimed that their Aryan ancestors had sought refuge in the Himalayas during a mythical cataclysmic ice age.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E3A chronological telling of the dramatic D-Day story, focusing on vessels that made the landings possible. From the X-Craft lying on the seabed days before the invasion to battleships like USS Texas and HMS Belfast that bombarded the Normandy beaches.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E4We pinpoint the moment the USA became a global superpower when we recreate how the USS Olympia won the Battle of Manila Bay, and we show how the revolutionary British HMS Dreadnought brought ship design into the 20th century.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E1As the Nazis rose to power, Himmler and the SS were convinced Atlantis could be found, and instigated a series of archeological expeditions seeking to uncover and exploit its secrets.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E2Convinced the medieval witch trials were a Judeo-Christian attempt to exterminate the Aryans, Himmler established a special team led by Reinhard Heydrich to build a database of medieval German witchcraft practices.

programme.title: Iconic Combat Machines
programme.desc: E5The Soviet Union produced a large variety of tanks and airplanes during World War II. What made the T34 and the Chaika stand out and become icons?

programme.title: Iconic Combat Machines
programme.desc: E6Two of the fastest combat aircraft of World War 2, their origins couldn't differ more. The Messerschmitt 262 was the brainchild of genius designer Willy Messerschmitt and it became the first combat jet in history.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E5The debate about humanity's true origins becomes a nefarious fixation as SS leader Heinrich Himmler turns his attention to proving the Paleolithic past of Germany's Aryan race.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E6Runes are the letters of an ancient Germanic writing system that harkens back to a mythological age filled with heroes, magic, and mystery.

programme.title: Nazi Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: E1As the Nazis waged a war of destruction across Europe, women travelling on Berlin’s S-Bahn train network were being stalked in the carriages at night. During the wartime blackouts, a serial killer used the darkness to carry out a reign of terror.

programme.title: Nazi Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: E2In 1943, the mysterious murder of one of the wealthiest men in the British empire, Sir Harry Oakes, sparked a chain of events that have led many to believe that the Duke of Windsor had not learned from his mistakes.

programme.title: WWII Battles In Colour

programme.title: WWII Battles In Colour
